events.text: a budget law that reduced national funding for public health coverage for low-income residents by about 14 percent over ten years and added work requirements to that coverage. The official estimate is that about 3 percent of residents lose health coverage as a result

a three-year extension of expanded premium subsidies for individually purchased health insurance. About 7 percent of residents hold that insurance, and an independent estimate was that subsidized buyers' average premium payment would more than double without the extension

a bill that loosened rules for employer and association health plans and funded payments that reduce cost sharing in individual insurance. The official estimate was that it would lower pre-subsidy premiums for individual insurance by about 11 percent and reduce the number of residents with coverage by about 0.03 percent
the same budget law, which also reduced national funding for food assistance for low-income households by about 16 percent over ten years

a law that raises the standard rate of the main benefit for working-age people above inflation for four years, which the government estimated would raise income for about one in seven households, and that cuts the benefit's health-related supplement by about half for new applicants, leaving current recipients and people with the most severe lifelong conditions unaffected

a law removing the rule that limited child-related benefit payments to a family's first two children. The government estimated that the change reaches about one in ten children and lifts about 3 percent of all children out of poverty

a health insurance savings law that raised patient charges for medicines by half, restricted free coverage of spouses under public health insurance, and curbed payment increases to doctors, hospitals, and drug makers, in order to hold contribution rates steady
a pension law that holds the public pension at 48 percent of average wages through 2031 and adds six months of pension entitlement per child for parents of children born before 1992

a reform that replaced the main basic income benefit, which about 7 percent of residents receive, with a stricter scheme: benefit rates stay the same, benefits are cut by 30 percent for three months for refusing training and cut for one month after a second missed appointment, and full withdrawal can follow further missed appointments
a suspension of a law raising the retirement age, which freezes that age until 2028
the annual social insurance budget, which carried that suspension and dropped a planned freeze on pensions and minimum benefits
the annual budget, which continued the public dental plan, public drug coverage, and subsidized child care without adding new funding for them
the same annual budget, which also made a national school meals program permanent
